report.summary: Chunk 8 of 11 of daedalus/structcore/parse.py: contains functions for generic splitting, annotation checks, union ID generation, and helper functions for declaration classification.

handoff.purpose: Provides utility functions for generic type splitting, annotation checking, and declaration kind classification.

symbols.name: split_generic
symbols.note: Uses lru_cache, parses raw string into AST, returns tuple of container and element texts.

symbols.name: is_any_annotation
symbols.note: Checks if normalized annotation is Any.

symbols.name: union_id
symbols.note: Generates stable group ID for union site edges.

symbols.name: _decl_kind
symbols.note: Classifies ClassDef into typeddict, namedtuple, enum, protocol, dataclass, or class.

symbols.name: _decorator_texts
symbols.note: Returns tuple of unparsed decorator texts.

symbols.name: _base_texts
symbols.note: Returns tuple of unparsed base and keyword texts.

symbols.name: _params_of
symbols.note: Returns parameters in reading order and receiver candidate name.

claims.text: One level of generic: ``(container spelling, element texts)``.
claims.why: The function returns a tuple of (container, element_texts).

claims.text: ``list[User]`` -> ``("list", ("User",))``; ``dict[str, User]`` -> ``("dict", ("User",))`` because a mapping's KEY is not its element; ``Callable[[int], User]`` -> ``("Callable", ("User",))``.
claims.why: The examples are not executed in this chunk; the logic for _slice_elements, _dotted_tail, annotation_text, and the constants _CALLABLE_NAMES, _MAP_CONTAINERS, _SEQ_CONTAINERS are not defined here.

claims.text: A bare nominal is ``("", (raw,))``, and an unknown generic is ``("", ("MyGeneric[int]",))`` -- no container, because we refuse to guess that an unrecognised subscript is a container at all.
claims.why: The function returns ('', (text,)) when node is not a Subscript or when tail is not recognized.

claims.text: True for a bare ``Any``/``typing.Any`` -- the sentinel a caller must refuse to edge to. ``dict[str, Any]`` is NOT bare Any; it is a dict whose element type is unknown, which is a different fact and a different number.
claims.why: The function depends on normalize_annotation which is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: Stable group id shared by every member edge of ONE union SITE.
claims.why: The function returns a string based on module, owner, role, param, which is stable.

claims.text: Derived entirely from the site's identity, never from a counter over a set or dict: a counter would renumber whenever iteration order shifted, and two processes would then disagree byte-for-byte on an id that is supposed to mean 'these edges are alternatives to each other'.
claims.why: The function returns an f-string using the parameters, no counter involved.

claims.text: Base-derived kinds win over decorator-derived ones, because a base changes what the declaration IS (a TypedDict is a dict shape, an Enum's members are values) while ``@dataclass`` only changes what is generated for it.
claims.why: The function checks bases before decorators, returning 'typeddict', 'namedtuple', 'enum', 'protocol' before checking for dataclass.

claims.text: Fixed order, so the answer never depends on dict order.
claims.why: The function uses a fixed sequence of if-elif checks, not dependent on set/dict iteration order.

claims.text: Parameters in reading order, plus the receiver candidate name.
claims.why: The function body is incomplete in this chunk; the full implementation is not present.
